# google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model

A model deployed to a Vertex AI Endpoint.

Deploying a model with this resource does not assign prediction traffic.
Manage the endpoint-wide `traffic_split` with `google_vertex_ai_endpoint`
or another endpoint traffic controller, but not both. Because the endpoint
must exist before a model can be deployed, first apply the endpoint and
deployment without a traffic split, then configure the split and apply
again. Use the known `deployed_model_id` in the endpoint's split instead
of a reference to this resource, which would create a dependency cycle.

When a model that shares traffic is deleted, its share is redistributed to
the remaining models in proportion to their current share, atomically as
part of the undeploy request. If the model is the only one receiving
traffic, deletion clears the split using the endpoint's etag before
undeploying it, stopping prediction traffic. This requires permission to
update the endpoint. If the endpoint remains managed, also update its
`traffic_split` configuration so it no longer references the deleted model.


To get more information about EndpointDeployedModel, see:

* [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.endpoints/deployModel)
* How-to Guides
    * [Deploy a model to an endpoint](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/general/deployment)
    * [Undeploy a model](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.endpoints/undeployModel)
    * [Update a deployed model](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.endpoints/mutateDeployedModel)


## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Endpoint Deployed Model Basic


```hcl
# After deploying the model, configure the endpoint's traffic_split in a
# separate apply to route prediction traffic to this deployed model.
resource "google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model" "deployed_model" {
  endpoint          = google_vertex_ai_endpoint.endpoint.id
  deployed_model_id = "1234567890"
  model             = google_vertex_ai_model.model.id

  dedicated_resources {
    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n1-standard-2"
    }

    min_replica_count = 1
    max_replica_count = 1
  }
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_endpoint" "endpoint" {
  name         = "endpoint-name"
  display_name = "Terraform deployed model endpoint"
  location     = "us-central1"
  region       = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_model" "model" {
  model_id     = "model-id"
  project      = "my-project-name"
  region       = "us-central1"
  source_model = "projects/my-project-name/locations/us-central1/models/my-source-model"
}
```

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Endpoint Deployed Model Shared Resources


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model" "deployed_model" {
  endpoint          = google_vertex_ai_endpoint.endpoint.id
  deployed_model_id = "1234567890"
  model             = google_vertex_ai_model.model.id
  shared_resources  = google_vertex_ai_deployment_resource_pool.pool.id

  # Deployment resource pools enable container logging, and a model deployed
  # to a pool must use the same setting.
  enable_container_logging = true
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_deployment_resource_pool" "pool" {
  name   = "deployed-model-pool"
  region = "us-central1"

  dedicated_resources {
    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n1-standard-2"
    }

    min_replica_count = 1

  }

  project      = "my-project-name"

}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `deployed_model_id` -
  (Required)
  The user-specified ID of the DeployedModel. The ID must contain 1 to 10
  numeric characters and must be unique among the models deployed to the Endpoint.

* `model` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the Model to deploy. The resource name may include a
  version ID or version alias, for example
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/models/{model}@2`.

* `endpoint` -
  (Required)
  The Endpoint to deploy the Model to, in the format
  `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}`.


* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The display name of the DeployedModel. If omitted, the Model's display name is used.

* `service_account` -
  (Optional)
  The service account that the DeployedModel's container runs as. The user
  deploying the Model must have the `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` permission
  on this service account.

* `enable_access_logging` -
  (Optional)
  Whether online prediction access logs are sent to Cloud Logging.

* `enable_container_logging` -
  (Optional)
  Whether container `stderr` and `stdout` logging is enabled. This is only
  supported for custom-trained Models and AutoML Tabular Models. If unset,
  the API default is used (enabled in the `google` provider, disabled in
  the `google-beta` provider).

* `dedicated_resources` -
  (Optional)
  Dedicated resources used by the DeployedModel.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources).

* `shared_resources` -
  (Optional)
  The shared DeploymentResourcePool to deploy on, in the format
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/deploymentResourcePools/{deployment_resource_pool}`.

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region of the Endpoint.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_dedicated_resources"></a>The `dedicated_resources` block supports:

* `machine_spec` -
  (Required)
  The specification of a single machine used by the deployment.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources_machine_spec).

* `min_replica_count` -
  (Required)
  The minimum number of machine replicas that will always be deployed.

* `max_replica_count` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum number of machine replicas that may be deployed.

* `required_replica_count` -
  (Optional)
  The number of available replicas required for the deployment operation
  to succeed. If omitted, this defaults to `min_replica_count`.

* `spot` -
  (Optional)
  Whether to schedule the deployment workload on Spot VMs.

* `autoscaling_metric_specs` -
  (Optional)
  Autoscaling metrics for the deployment.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources_autoscaling_metric_specs).


<a name="nested_dedicated_resources_machine_spec"></a>The `machine_spec` block supports:

* `machine_type` -
  (Optional)
  The machine type used by each replica. Defaults to `n1-standard-2`.

* `accelerator_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type of accelerator attached to the machine. See the
  [supported accelerator types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/Shared.Types/AcceleratorType).

* `accelerator_count` -
  (Optional)
  The number of accelerators attached to the machine.

<a name="nested_dedicated_resources_autoscaling_metric_specs"></a>The `autoscaling_metric_specs` block supports:

* `metric_name` -
  (Required)
  The resource metric name.

* `target` -
  (Optional)
  The target resource utilization percentage for the metric. When
  first omitted, the API defaults this to 60. To reset an existing
  target to 60, set it explicitly; removing it from the configuration
  retains the existing value.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}`

* `model_version_id` -
  The version ID of the deployed Model.

* `create_time` -
  The timestamp when the DeployedModel was created.

* `private_endpoints` -
  Private paths for sending requests to the deployed model.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_private_endpoints).


<a name="nested_private_endpoints"></a>The `private_endpoints` block contains:

* `predict_http_uri` -
  (Output)
  The HTTP path for prediction requests.

* `explain_http_uri` -
  (Output)
  The HTTP path for explanation requests.

* `health_http_uri` -
  (Output)
  The HTTP path for health check requests.

* `service_attachment` -
  (Output)
  The service attachment resource used by Private Service Connect.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following

- `create` - Default is 60 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 60 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 60 minutes.

## Import


EndpointDeployedModel can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import EndpointDeployedModel using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    deployedModelId = "<-required value->"
    endpoint = "<-required value->"
    region = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import EndpointDeployedModel using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), EndpointDeployedModel can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
```
